notes.title: Post-Release Update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38662450/c987f0ae3e859625434960655afe4aad6a721eda.png[/img]

[b]Diagnosis: Update! [/b]

Since Healing Spree’s launch, we’ve been in awe of your hilarious streams, screenshots and social media posts! Though you are all untrained, you are quickly mastering your skills in medical negligence. 

Now, the development team are back to share more about our upcoming roadmap, including key updates and fixes!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38662450/ba09053bdfe5b2b804cfc653f097814130d40557.png[/img]

[b]1. Networking[/b]

A few of you might have experienced connection issues; let us explain more about it. Healing Spree is a fast-paced, action multiplayer game with throw/collision physics. To deliver the best experience, we decided to synchronize everything in real-time. All the actions, objects you throw, and collisions are synced through the network in real-time. 

This is a huge challenge for us as it requires a super low latency environment with every object and action synced similar to some hardcore action games. In development, we changed the whole structure 3 times. We went from P2P(peer-to-peer) to dedicated servers, then back to P2P. The reason we are using P2P instead is that we are unable to set up servers around the world. P2P through Steam handles such situations better. 85% of players have a better experience in our beta test through P2P.

To summarize, players should let someone who has the best connection be the host and make sure they are not behind a firewall. 

Our team knows exactly how frustrating a connection problem is, as we are all gamers too. We’ll make sure that enhancing game connection will be one of our top priorities in the upcoming patch.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38662450/4ccc6a6c5d021c0cade924542f86a6e3e1cbe88e.png[/img]

[b]2. Controls[/b]

We’ve also received your feedback about the game controls and we’re aware that the [b]use[/b] and  [b]throw[/b] actions in Overcooked are mapped in the same button. However, In Healing Spree, the two buttons are separated. This might take a while in getting used to but allows more flexibility in certain scenarios. The reason behind this is that we have decided to allow players to [b]throw everything[/b]. This is different for Overcooked since some items cannot be thrown (like the fire extinguisher) as the button only allows one action at a time.

We believe that allowing players to throw everything in the game would create more strategies and choices in the long run. Therefore, we decided to keep the controls as is. Remember that controls can be rebound to better suit everyone’s playstyle. 

We are also working on enhancing control sensitivity and item snapping. Our priority would be enhancing your control and overall gaming experience. With your reports, we can keep improving the game and grow together with our players.

We will upload a new patch with fixes soon! So stay tuned to our future updates on [url=https://twitter.com/HealingSpreeHQ]Twitter[/url], [url=https://www.instagram.com/healingspreegame]Instagram, [/url][url=https://www.facebook.com/HealingSpree]Facebook [/url]and our [url=http://healing-spree.com/]Website[/url].

Join our community of (untrained) medical professionals on [url=https://discord.gg/mBxjC86wRB]Discord[/url] too to find games, seek support, or just share your hilarious streams.

Till next time!

Paro

notes.title: Healing Spree - Dev log
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38662450/ff9405ae1dcdfde2b84f3155de81eb49f5f7c87f.png[/img]

Calling all doctors! 

We have been hard at work here in the hospital! Day and night we’ve been fixing, polishing and cleaning the hospital for viruses(bugs) and making sure that the Co-Op feature is ready to go. We wouldn’t want our doctors to be disorganized while operating on a patient! 

We believe that our doctors should be updated with the work and improvements during our hospital’s development. Especially since the launch is just around the corner on October 20th!

With that aside, every time we add something, old stuff stops working. This is why our QA time turned into an insanely long process. Latency is a huge issue in Co-Op and we have been working tirelessly to improve that feature. We do not intend to stop until it is absolutely seamless!

Let’s dive into a detailed log and chat about some of the work done on the game recently!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38662450/ba09053bdfe5b2b804cfc653f097814130d40557.png[/img]

[b][u]Networking Issues[/u][/b]

Players requested networking fixes and we started working on this roughly a year ago. Only recently were we able to iron out the main issues. Maintaining QA has been a challenge as we are a small team. To be able to do testing successfully, we will need players coming from all around the world to do a Co-Op stress test for the overall performance of Co-Op mode. Whenever we add features in the multiplayer, we also have to tweak our physics system, which is one of the usual things we end up having to patch.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38662450/cea70fc62fc8ffe0618f0fbc2386ecaeee7d47c7.png[/img]

[b][u]Physics Issues, Game Balancing and New Stages[/u][/b]

As they are all connected, we grouped the 3 major changes into this one section. Technically if you’ve played the demo, anything beyond chapter 1 is new. We have been testing these stages over and over again and saw that most of them were actually pretty hard to beat. Plus one of the biggest hindrances that we had were the game physics not responding as we would like it to.

Chapter 3
The boats in this chapter have some glitch issues. They tend to overlap and disrupt game physics. We had to adjust the weight and remove some realistic physics to create fake physics that makes it playable.

Chapter 4
The fan in stage 4-4 is a big issue, it took us forever to tune it properly. This mechanic is a huge fan which you can apply force to push. Initially, it was too heavy, and it had a weird bug that caused the fan to become loose due to physics being too close to a real fan. So once again, we had to make some “fake physics” magic happen.

Chapter 5
We had a lot of trouble balancing the fire. Players often find themselves caught in flames and end up spreading it everywhere. We made the dash mechanic work to remove the fire, so you can dash and put those flames out! A few of the stages here have also been rebalanced to make it a little bit easier to play. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38662450/667826fbb6657cad1346d0537ce6a74c5a794ab6.png[/img]

[b][u]Other stuff[/u][/b]

Story:
Save everyone from infectminator (infect me later) by combining forces and uniting the multiverse. Travel through earth, animal-verse, the fiery depths, frozen kingdom, and alien invasions to save everyone. By bringing them back to life, it makes the conflict meaningless.

Older Development Work:
The game was actually simpler and leaned more towards Overcooked, whereby the game required you to mix different types of pills and medicine. We decided to change the direction to map mechanics and less of the medicine mixing to ensure we had a unique vibe to our game.

Memes:
Look for the special memes and references in our game! We pay tribute to all the references that inspired us throughout the game development. Coffin dance, pewdiepie, and all sorts of other referenced characters in animation. See if you can find them all!

Family-Friendly Mode:
Find the game too hard? We have added a family-friendly mode that everyone can enjoy, with lowered score requirements and higher points when you save a patient.

And thats it! Don't forget, you can always join our [url=https://discord.gg/4CceEYfk7k]discord [/url]and follow our social medias for up to date announcements!

notes.title: Brand New Closed Beta Test!
notes.content:
Get your fire extinguishers - I mean - patient beds ready, doctors. 

We're holding a brand new Closed Beta Test, from September 10th at 8AM CST to September 13th at 8PM CST.

If you've always wanted to throw around and cut open *ahem* treat and care Healing Spree's patients, now's your chance! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38662450/13237f318e60d6c425abdaaa6bddb70e03a93115.png[/img]

Simply sign up in our [url=https://discord.gg/tCXs7zfQTK]discord channel[/url], before September 8th at 11:59 pm CST. Be sure to fill out the form in the #beta-registration channel in our discord so that we can send you the key(s) via email. Please do report any bugs you may encounter, and leave any suggestions or feedback that you may have. This information is essential for the improvement of future patches, and we cannot thank you enough! 

You may request up to 3 extra keys to give to friends, to play in our hilariously chaotic co-op mode! If you would like extra keys for your friends, this MUST be stated within your registration form. 

We are so excited to have you join us and cannot wait to see the crazy stories from you and your friends! If there are any further questions regarding the Beta, please feel free to ask us either in the comments here or on [url=https://discord.gg/tCXs7zfQTK]Discord[/url]. 

See you in our hospital soon!

notes.title: The “throw” mechanic of Healing Spree.
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/5ztIeyP.gif[/img]

We loved Overcooked and one of the game changer in OC2  is the throw mechanism. 

Fun up at least 300% with it, no joke. That’s why we decided to let players throw almost everything in our game with some interesting physics. 

Although it also came with 500% debug and testing time. (Man, those physics bugs and interaction are annoying.)

Some items interact and behave differently, you guys can try it in our upcoming demo version later. 
Remember to throw things through the tiny window and tell us what you think, we made a window throw assist function just for that.

notes.title: The Myth of Healing Spree
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/y4mo24I.gif[/img]

This is H from Paro. The raging dev who likes making games. I am gonna share some not too important dev stuff here, it's purely for emotional release. Skip it if you want.

In short, we are broken people that hate lives and the world, so we originally designed a zombie infection coop game with 4 people running around infecting the whole city.

It was called “Killing Spree”. 

Although we liked the idea of going rampage. The game was not friendship breaking enough, so we were not happy about the design.

We started yelling at each other because we weren’t yelling at each other. 
The design was breaking our friendship but not the game, and that’s bad, very bad.
 
So we shifted the design.
